arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Marwell argued that common law burglary requires trespass for a crime.
Mr. Tripp argued that the conviction qualifies under the ACCA text.
Justice Ginsburg noted that Taylor suggests few statutes are broader than the generic definition.
Justice Alito questioned why the Court would examine statutes without a remaining-in element.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of the Armed Career Criminal Act. It asks if a state conviction qualifies as a predicate offense. The definition of generic burglary drives the outcome.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to exclude his conviction from the ACCA count.
The government wants the Court to include his conviction in the ACCA count.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that generic burglary requires proof of remaining inside a structure.
The government argues that the statutory text alone defines the qualifying offense.
